Selected publications are grouped by the research applications they demonstrate. Metadata and links were checked against PubMed and publisher records.

## Featured Applications

::: {.card-grid}
::: {.publication-card}
### A single-amino-acid cleavage controls global mitochondrial complex integrity
**Kücükköse C. et al. 2026.** *Nature Structural & Molecular Biology*. [DOI: 10.1038/s41594-026-01876-7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41594-026-01876-7) | [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42675210/)

An application of quantitative complexome profiling to show that loss of ICP55-mediated removal of one N-terminal amino acid causes widespread destabilization of human mitochondrial protein assemblies.
:::

::: {.publication-card}
### Distinct Assembly Complexes Facilitate cbb~3~-type Cytochrome Oxidase Maturation
**Shen K. et al. 2026.** *Journal of Molecular Biology* 438(19):169945. [DOI: 10.1016/j.jmb.2026.169945](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jmb.2026.169945) | [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42447953/)

An application of complexome profiling to resolve stable bacterial cytochrome oxidase assembly intermediates and their roles in coordinated heme and copper insertion.
:::

::: {.publication-card}
### Fractionated proteomics identifies a protein network mitigating resistance exercise-induced damage in human skeletal muscle
**Kuppusamy M. et al. 2026.** *Nature Communications* 17:7110. [DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-75501-y](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-75501-y) | [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42521682/)

Fractionated human muscle proteomics and phosphoproteomics identify a BAG3-linked network involved in adaptation to resistance exercise. The companion [Quarto/R analysis project](projects/bag3-fractionated-proteomics/) makes the missing-value imputation and differential-abundance workflow available for reuse.
:::
:::

## Established Selected Publications

::: {.publication-card}
### TermineR: Extracting information on endogenous proteolytic processing from shotgun proteomics data
**Cosenza-Contreras M. et al. 2024.** *Proteomics* 24(19). [DOI: 10.1002/pmic.202300491](https://doi.org/10.1002/pmic.202300491)

Software and method paper connected to the [TermineR](https://github.com/MiguelCos/TermineR) R package. It reflects Miguel's work on turning shotgun proteomics data into interpretable information on endogenous proteolytic processing.
:::

::: {.publication-card}
### Proteometabolomics of initial and recurrent glioblastoma highlights an increased immune cell signature with altered lipid metabolism
**Cosenza-Contreras M. et al. 2024.** *Neuro-Oncology* 26(3):488-502. [DOI: 10.1093/neuonc/noad208](https://doi.org/10.1093/neuonc/noad208)

Clinical proteomics and multi-omics integration study combining proteomics, lipidomics, proteogenomics, and clinical interpretation in recurrent glioblastoma.
:::

::: {.publication-card}
### The Schistosomiasis SpleenOME: Unveiling the Proteomic Landscape of Splenomegaly Using Label-Free Mass Spectrometry
**Cosenza-Contreras M. et al. 2018/2019.** *Frontiers in Immunology* 9:3137. [DOI: 10.3389/fimmu.2018.03137](https://doi.org/10.3389/fimmu.2018.03137)

Host-parasite interaction and label-free proteomics study from Miguel's earlier work in biological sciences and proteomics.
:::

::: {.publication-card}
### Proteome alterations in human autopsy tissues in relation to time after death
**Kocsmar E., Schmid M., Cosenza-Contreras M. et al. 2023.** *Cellular and Molecular Life Sciences* 80:117. [DOI: 10.1007/s00018-023-04754-3](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00018-023-04754-3)

Tissue proteomics study relevant to degradation, translational sample quality, and interpretation of post-mortem tissue proteomes.
:::
